what: Apollo Global Management invests in credit and private equity, and owns Athene, a retirement services company that sells annuities. The annuity money gives it permanent capital to lend, which is the engine of the whole firm.
customers: Institutional investors in its funds, companies borrowing from its credit arm, and savers buying Athene annuities.
money: Athene annuities and the investment income on the assets backing them
management fees on credit, private equity and real asset funds
its own capital invested alongside clients, and performance fees
moat: Permanent capital from annuities that it never has to raise again, combined with origination platforms that create loans other investors cannot buy.
risks: Reported earnings swing with accounting marks on the annuity book and can show a loss
Credit losses in private lending would hit both the funds and Athene
Annuity sales depend on interest rates staying attractive to savers
Private credit is drawing heavy competition and spreads are narrowing
opportunities: Fee-related earnings and spread income are recurring and have grown steadily
Companies are borrowing from private lenders rather than banks, which is its core market
Origination volume keeps rising, which feeds both the funds and Athene
watch: Fee-related earnings and spread-related earnings, which are the recurring parts, rather than reported net income.
